transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. We have a block of distressed municipal bonds on the table -- $12 million face value, currently quoted at 82 cents on the dollar, maturing in 30 months. Before I record a vote, I'd like to hear from each of you per our normal pre-trade procedure. Let's start with credit risk -- what are your conditions or implementation requirements? Then we'll move to legal, markets, and accounting in turn.

transcript.text: Elena, before we go around the table, I want to flag a liquidity constraint from my end. I confirmed with the execution desk today that we cannot buy more than $5 million of these bonds over four trading days without causing material market impact. That's a hard limit from a trading perspective, and it's directly relevant to how we size this -- the full $12 million face value at 82 cents would be roughly $9.84 million, which exceeds what the desk says we can execute without moving the market against ourselves. I'll have the desk's liquidity note available for the committee if needed.

transcript.text: Before we go further, I need to flag a single-issuer concentration issue. I confirmed in the exposure report I reviewed this morning that the bank already has $4 million of exposure to this issuer, and the applicable single-issuer limit is $10 million. That position has not yet been added to the committee packet, so you may not have seen it. What this means is that if we were to purchase the full $12 million face value at 82 cents -- roughly $9.84 million -- our total exposure to this issuer would come to approximately $13.84 million, which would breach the $10 million single-issuer limit by nearly $4 million. Even accounting for Hassan's liquidity constraint of $5 million over four trading days, adding $5 million to our existing $4 million would bring us to $9 million, which is within the limit but leaves only $1 million of headroom. My condition is that any purchase must be sized so that total exposure to this issuer remains at or below $10 million, and I will update the committee packet with the existing exposure figure before the vote is recorded.

transcript.text: Before we move to the vote, I need to flag an accounting classification issue. While reviewing the bond terms this week, I determined that the contractual cash flows include a contingent step-up feature. Under our accounting framework, that means this position cannot be held at amortized cost -- it must be recorded at fair value through profit or loss. I have a memo documenting this conclusion that I was planning to circulate, but given where we are in the discussion, I want the committee to be aware now so that everyone understands the P&L volatility implications before Elena records the vote. My implementation requirement is that the position be classified as FVTPL from day one, and I'll finalize and circulate the accounting memo to the committee packet.

transcript.text: Elena, before we move to the vote, I need to flag a settlement requirement from a transfer-agent memo I received this afternoon. This bond block may settle only after the buyer provides a beneficial-owner certification and uses an approved municipal-bond custodian. I have not yet attached the memo to the trade file, but I will do so before the vote is recorded. My implementation requirements are twofold: first, the purchase authorization should be conditioned on our ability to provide the beneficial-owner certification, and second, settlement must be arranged through an approved municipal-bond custodian. If either condition cannot be met, the trade should not proceed.
